{"subject":"Tail latency on a self-managed Cassandra fleet","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. Your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard stuck with me, especially the work on tail latency and GC/compaction tuning.

That tuning burden is the problem ScyllaDB's design targets: a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, so p99 latency stays predictable without chasing GC settings.

If it's useful, I'm happy to share how that maps to a leaderboard-style workload like yours.

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB
